  • Initial vomiting (resolved)  
  • Intermittent left-sided lower abdominal cramps  
  • Subjective fever at illness onset; feels weak/shaky  
  • Recent takeaway (Chinese restaurant) 4 days ago – possible food-borne trigger

Management Plan

- Working diagnosis: Likely viral gastroenteritis (possible food-borne etiology).
- Advice/education:
  • Rest at home and avoid work for 2–3 days.  
  • Maintain hydration with water and oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
  • Light diet as tolerated.  
  • Paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to QID PRN for fever or discomfort.
- Red flags/when to return:
  • If symptoms persist >3–4 days, worsen, or new features develop (blood in stool, high fever, dehydration).  
  • Plan for stool sample and further tests if no improvement.
- No antibiotics prescribed at this stage.
- Sick note for employer if required (not specifically requested).
- Follow-up: Review in 3–4 days or earlier if concerned.
